assessments.zone: Rural villages of Aungba, Kambala and Rimba health zones away from the Djugu border
assessments.evidence: Calm Alur rural areas with customary chiefs and police/administration from Mahagi, Nioka and Aru; no reported armed-group control. Web research could not be performed for this unit (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked); assessment is inference from background knowledge to mid-2026.

assessments.zone: Western Aungba and Kambala border villages towards Djugu (Kepira, Zani, Aupa, Ngbiki, Wadaka, Udju, Berunda health areas)
assessments.evidence: Alur villages on the western edge of Mahagi territory adjoining Djugu's Lendu areas; state administration and police remain, with FARDC positions on the border, while CODECO raids from Djugu are a recurrent risk rather than an established presence. Web research could not be performed for this unit (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked); assessment is inference from background knowledge to mid-2026. Reviewer: the western Aungba health-zone areas (Djalasiga, Zani, Kepira, Aupa, Ngbiki, Wadaka) are believed to fall largely in the Lendu-populated Walendu Watsi secteur, where CODECO influence may be greater than assumed here; could not be verified.

assessments.zone: Main towns of Rimba, Kambala and Aungba areas (Nioka/Pandoro, Cité Lopka, Jupadhi, Jupacen, Jupalang'u, Jupamalawi, Rona centre, Reru, Juru, Kambi)
assessments.evidence: Northern/central Mahagi (Alur chefferies) has seen no established armed-group control; Nioka and the RN27 towns host state administration, PNC posts and FARDC detachments. Web research could not be performed for this unit (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked); assessment is inference from background knowledge to mid-2026. Reviewer: status lowered from exclusive to dominant since no source confirms absence of armed actors.

assessments.zone: Djalasiga gold-mining centre (Akwerali settlement and Djalasiga health area, Aungba health zone)
assessments.evidence: Djalasiga is a large artisanal gold-mining agglomeration in north-western Mahagi, administered by the state with police and a military detachment guarding the mining area; CODECO elements from neighbouring Djugu (Walendu Tatsi/Watsi) have historically made incursions into western Mahagi mining sites but are not known to hold the town. Web research could not be performed for this unit (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked); assessment is inference from background knowledge to mid-2026. Reviewer: the western Aungba health-zone areas (Djalasiga, Zani, Kepira, Aupa, Ngbiki, Wadaka) are believed to fall largely in the Lendu-populated Walendu Watsi secteur, where CODECO influence may be greater than assumed here; could not be verified.

assessments.zone: Angumu health zone (Mokambo/Panduru area, Lake Albert hinterland): Angumu town and its health areas, Rakpa, Anzika, Ramogi, Logo-HZ villages south of 2.10N (Alasi, Walla, Gomandri…)
assessments.evidence: Southern Mahagi (Angumu area) borders CODECO strongholds in Djugu and has experienced CODECO attacks and displacement since 2019-2023, prompting FARDC deployments; the army is assessed as the main force, with CODECO raids. Low confidence; no current sources could be consulted.

assessments.zone: Southwestern edge of Angumu next to Djugu border (Luru, Mbila, Yissa 1 – Musongwa/Terali health areas)
assessments.evidence: These villages lie on the edge of the Rethy/Walendu Pitsi CODECO zone in Djugu; FARDC presence is contested by CODECO incursions. Low-confidence inference.

assessments.zone: Alur heartland: Logo, Nyarambe towns and rural villages of Mahagi, Logo and Nyarambe health zones (Alur chefferies north of the Djugu border)
assessments.evidence: The northern and central Alur-majority parts of Mahagi territory are largely outside the CODECO conflict zone, which is concentrated in southern Mahagi (Djugu border) and Djugu; state police and administration operate in Logo, Nyarambe and surrounding villages. Assessment by default state presence; no web research could be done.

assessments.zone: Western Mahagi uplands near the Djugu (Walendu Pitsi) border: Rimba and Aungba health-zone villages in the unit (Jupabong, Jupadrogo, Pamitu, Uwilo, Lualu, God Awisi…)
assessments.evidence: Rimba/Aungba areas lie closer to the Lendu–Alur/Hema conflict zone and have seen sporadic CODECO incursions in recent years, but the larger villages remain under state police/FARDC. Low-confidence inference without fresh sources.

assessments.zone: Mahagi town (cité, all neighbourhoods), Mahagi Douane/Goli border area, Mahagi Port lakeshore (Caritas, Kolokoto)
assessments.evidence: Mahagi is the territorial capital and Uganda border/lake-port hub with permanent PNC, territorial administration and FARDC garrison; no reports of armed-group control of the town are known. No web research possible for this unit, so this is a default-presence assessment.

units.CD5407-mahagi-2: This unit covers northern Mahagi territory (Aungba, Kambala and Rimba health zones, mostly Alur chefferies around Nioka and towards Aru). Unlike southern Mahagi and neighbouring Djugu, the area is not known to be held by CODECO or other armed groups; the state (PNC with FARDC detachments, under customary chiefs locally) is treated as the controller. The western fringe bordering Djugu, including the Djalasiga gold-mining centre, is exposed to CODECO incursions and is rated lower confidence. NOTE: web research could not be performed for this unit (search budget exhausted, news/aggregator sites blocked), so all zones are inferences from background knowledge and should be re-checked. Reviewer note (2026-10-01): independent review also could not run web searches (budget exhausted) or fetch search engines/ReliefWeb (egress blocked); no claim could be verified against dated reports. Only change: the Rimba/Kambala towns zone (z3) was lowered from 'exclusive' to 'dominant' as overstated; western Aungba (Walendu Watsi, Lendu-populated) is flagged as the area most likely to need correction toward CODECO influence.
units.CD5407-mahagi-1: Mahagi territory part 1 (Mahagi, Logo, Nyarambe and Angumu health zones) is mostly Alur-majority and lies north/east of the Djugu Hema–Lendu conflict core. Mahagi town, the Uganda border/lake port and Logo/Nyarambe are assessed as state-held (PNC with FARDC). The southern Angumu area and the western Rimba/Aungba fringe border CODECO zones and suffer incursions; FARDC is assessed as the main force there. NOTE: no web research could be done for this unit (search budget exhausted, sites blocked); all zones are default-presence or low-confidence inferences and should be re-checked. Reviewer note (2026-10-01): independent review also could not run web searches or fetch news sites (search budget exhausted, egress blocked); zones were checked only for internal consistency and against the neighbouring Djugu and Mahagi-2 assessments. The cited sources (s1-s3) are generic portals, not specific reports.
